text: The design is built. Now it gets tested the real way — defended out loud, against a panel that pushes back on every choice this capstone has made.

First challenge: why not just give each hospital system its own instance, given how autonomous they've always been? The real defense names the actual test from Chapter 2 — Meridian has neither a data-residency requirement nor true business-unit independence — and points out that three instances would pay the upgrade and security multiplier three times over, forever. The autonomy concern is real, but it's a governance problem, already solved by a federated governance model, not a reason to build three of everything.

Second challenge: how does this scale if a fourth hospital system joins in two years? A strong answer doesn't oversell it. Adding a domain is a bounded, known pattern, far cheaper than a fourth full instance — but it's not free. Each additional domain compounds the overhead of testing every script and integration against it, so the honest recommendation is to revisit whether the domain count is still right, not to claim it scales for free forever.

Third challenge: why not make every integration consistently event-driven? The defense holds the line from Chapter 4 — neither pattern is categorically better. An HR rep waiting on a case screen needs an answer right now, which is exactly what request-response is for. And when the panel pushes on the security design looking too light in places, the answer holds again: uniform maximum restriction breeds shared logins and shadow spreadsheets. Controls stay strict where real risk justifies them, and fast everywhere else.

None of these are rehearsed lines — they're the actual tradeoffs this capstone worked through across three lessons, held up under direct challenge. That's the real skill: weighing real constraints, naming honest tradeoffs, and holding a reasoned position under pressure, which is the same judgment a real client engagement tests for the rest of a Technical Architect's career.

This course built that judgment. It isn't the credential itself — course 14, ServiceNow Career & Capstone, is next, and it turns everything built across this entire path toward your actual job search.
